meta.description: Parsa Derakhshan is a full-stack developer in Ottawa, building the Canadian Coast Guard's internal web applications in C#, .NET and Vue.

intro.p1: I'm a programmer analyst at the Canadian Coast Guard. I build the system that tracks Canada's buoys and other aids to navigation, and the internal apps staff use for pay, training and budgets, in C#/.NET and Vue.
intro.p2: On my own time I put language models to work on messy real data: a private search engine for my own immigration paperwork, and a reader that turns used-computer ads into prices.

inkplusbot.title: InkPlusBot
inkplusbot.meta: 2024 to now · C#, EF Core, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker
inkplusbot.body: A customer-facing Telegram bot for INK+, an Ottawa electronics repair and printing shop with three locations. It speaks English, French and Persian, finds ink and toner, gives repair estimates, lists refurbished devices and hands people over to staff. Product data comes from the INK+ website, which syncs from Lightspeed Retail. It runs in Docker on Linux, with Redis for conversation state and PostgreSQL for requests.

skiPatrol.title: Canadian Ski Patrol member system
skiPatrol.meta: 2023, college capstone · Java, Spring Boot, Hilla, Lit
skiPatrol.body: A college capstone that replaced the Canadian Ski Patrol's old Laravel/PHP member system, built for them as a real client. It has modules for events, training history, HR records and financial reports, each with a Java entity, a typed Hilla endpoint and a Lit view, and the interface is fully bilingual. It was handed to the Ski Patrol's contact, who deployed it to production.

experience.title: Experience

items.org: Canadian Coast Guard (Fisheries and Oceans Canada, now National Defence)
points: Designed the back end of ATONIS, which tracks Canada's buoys and other aids to navigation: a .NET 8 API using CQRS, on an Entity Framework model that follows the IHO S-201 standard.

Built its GraphQL API for map questions (what is inside this area, what is near this point) with GeoJSON export, and fixed a ring-orientation bug that made SQL Server return everything outside an area.
Built its Vue and Leaflet map, where staff draw and edit areas directly.
Moved FS3 to a new Azure DevOps project with rebuilt pipelines, and started bringing the 2007-era Fleet Safety System onto Razor Pages.
Also work on iPlan, the Pay Issue Portal, NTTT, PMIS and Activity Based Budgeting, tested from xUnit through integration tests on a real SQL Server to Selenium.
Wrote and tested Python scripts that automate the agency's yearly data update.
Built Power BI dashboards and analysis tools for researchers.
Helped update the Comparative Risk Model with data gathered alongside Statistics Canada and other agencies.
Built the research group's website from the first design, working from what they asked for.
Maintained the site and its database and added pages as needed, with every change tracked in Git.

rag.title: Private search over my immigration paperwork
rag.meta: 2026 · Swift (Apple Vision), Python, SQLite FTS5, pikepdf
rag.demoTitle: Try it: the same matching, on made-up documents
rag.caption: Eight invented documents for an invented applicant. The real index holds my own files and stays on my Mac.
rag.lead: The retrieval half of a RAG system over my own immigration (IRCC) paperwork.
points: Reads 745 files (scans, photos, passport stamps, letters and fillable IRCC forms, in English and Persian) the best way each allows: PDF text, Apple Vision OCR, or the typed answers inside the forms.
Indexes every page in SQLite full-text search and normalizes Persian digits and spellings. A date in any format also finds its other forms, Persian calendar included.
Measured, not guessed: a test set of 31 key facts only counts a fact when it is found in the file it should come from. It finds 30.
Runs entirely on my Mac. Next is the answer layer, which will cite the exact page behind every claim.

scout.title: Scout: reading used-computer ads with Claude
scout.meta: 2026 · C#, .NET 10, Anthropic SDK, Claude Haiku, PostgreSQL
scout.caption: From ReaderPrompt.cs: part of the instructions that keep model names consistent.
scout.lead: Scout works out what used laptops, tablets and desktops really sell for around Ottawa.
points: Claude Haiku reads every Marketplace, Kijiji, eBay and store listing once, again only if its text changes, and answers in JSON against a fixed schema: ad type, brand, family, exact model, configuration and condition.
The prompt carries the products already known, so the same machine always gets the same name. That part is cached across requests.
20 ads per request, 4 requests at a time, with the cost tracked on the status page: about ten cents per thousand listings.
The prompt and the parsing of answers are plain functions with unit tests, so they are tested without calling the model.

tools.title: Working with Claude Code
tools.body: I build with Claude Code and give it project rules it can't skip. For the INK+ website I wrote a /vibe-check skill that screenshots a page at phone and desktop sizes and audits it against our design rules, plus hooks that check every edit against the design and copy rules and block any commit that stages a secret file. This site went through the same checklist.
